note: Each value has the status EXCEPTION, NOT RELEASED. No human checked a value.
Each accuracy compares a method with the AI reference E20 v4.1, not with a human label.
A value is the text of the number as the source file stores it. The field display is the form for a reader: half-up to the decimals of the report.
A value that the tool read in a text can hold a thousands comma. The field value_plain is the same text with no comma. A reader that needs a number must read value_plain or display.

Paths are files of the private project. The field source.sha256_of says what the SHA-256 covers: the whole source file at the time of the field made, or the one line that holds the value (protocol, state file of the package: these files change often).
Group values_from_pdf: the product reads these 7 values from the PDF. The reference of these measures is the OpenParlData export, not a human label and not the AI reference.
An entry with the field opening_mark and the value 'after the opening' comes from a run after the one opening of the closed part: its rules were changed with knowledge of all development parliaments.

Round 4 (ids values.round4.*) is the product state: the rule files come from the PDF alone and the reader has rule V5. Round 3 (ids values.round3.*) is the earlier state: rule files with 3 export fields. Of the values file of round 4 the tool reads the key header only.

An entry with the field design_mark and the value 'after the design values of addendum I' is a value of the heads design (ids values.heads2.*): each head value is out-of-fold on development documents, and the design was made with knowledge of these values. Such a value is optimistic. It is not the measurement of the one last run.
An entry with the status 'not measured yet' has no value: its source file is not on disk. A text must not show such an entry as a result.
The mark 'reading check' is a judgement of an AI agent on 50 documents. It is not the measurement.
The field used_in is a plan of the AI agent that wrote the tool. No tool compared it with the texts.
A text can state a second calculation for a value only if second_calculation.equal is true.
The tool read aggregate records only. It dropped each key with values of single documents or single parliaments at the read. No value comes from a test document.

Marks: measured = a project script wrote the value into the source file; read = read in a document; protocol only = the value exists only in the text of the protocol; estimate = the source gives it as an estimate; derived = this tool calculated it from other entries or counted the items of a source key; reading check = an AI agent judged the value against the printed text.
The field second_calculation.done is true if a record or a protocol row states a second calculation by an AI agent. It does not say that a human checked the value.

The ids values.last_run.spread.* come from a file that was made after the one last run: they are information, not a measure of addendum I. The ids values.last_run.contact.* count id lists of earlier work, not the contact of an AI agent with a document. For an id file the tool counts the lines and copies no id.

steps: pandoc technical_report.md -s -o rep.tex --shift-heading-level-by=-1 -V geometry:a4paper,margin=15mm -V fontsize=10pt -V mainfont='Helvetica Neue' -V monofont=Menlo -V colorlinks=true -V linkcolor=black -V urlcolor=blue -H header.tex
remove the minipage wrappers of the table header cells in rep.tex
xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error rep.tex (one pass: with a second pass, longtable reused wrong column widths from the .aux file)

replaces.copied: the keys steps and header_tex of the key pdf; the other keys of pdf come from the build record of the PDF of form field 12
replaces.state: numbers.json replaces it for the numbers of the texts of 14.10.2026 and later. On 15.10.2026 the build of the website (web/build.py of the private project) still read its key numbers. Its key pdf gives the report PDF of 12.10.2026.
